page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 512 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with the stress-ng multi-core CPU test and PassMark CPU score both ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, achieving top-tier results in both small-block cached and large-block uncached read operations. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and PassMark memory scores falling into the average middle 50% category.

A key architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, meaning all storage operations rely on external Premium Storage. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive parallel compute and high memory bandwidth without the need for high-speed local NVMe drives. The server lacks dedicated GPU hardware, which limits its suitability for heavy graphics rendering or GPU-bound deep learning, though it demonstrates strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference prompt processing.

This server is suited for highly parallelized workloads such as large-scale database operations, static web serving, multi-threaded compression tasks, and CPU-based machine learning inference. Its high core count and memory bandwidth also make it appropriate for enterprise application hosting and containerized microservices architectures.
